verdict.rationale: Raygun documents ignore conditions for error groups: ignore for a time period, for a number of occurrences, or by rule. These directly cover the mute/ignore part of the story. Its pricing page lists 'Spike protection', but it is framed around flagging irregular data volumes to avoid surprise usage rather than suppressing alert pages, and nothing documents per-key rate limits. Missing for 10: per-key/per-error rate limiting of alerts, evidence that spike protection throttles notifications rather than just usage, documentation of ignore-by-rule depth, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can fight alert fatigue with spike protection, per-key rate limits, and mute/ignore rules so one bad deploy doesn't page the whole team all night

citations.quote: We provide three types of conditions: Ignore for a specific time period ... Ignore for a specific number of occurrences ... Ignore by rule
When you ignore an error group you can specify the condition you would like the error group to be ignored for.
Spike protection. Detect and flag irregular data volumes to avoid any surprise usage
